# `Browser.WebAuthn`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.WebAuthn — register and authenticate a public-key credential
from the browser via the Web Authentication API (`navigator.credentials`),
over `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

Two one-shot ceremonies span BOTH port directions: an outbound `JsCmd`
(`register` / `authenticate`) requests the ceremony, and a correlated inbound
`JsMsg` carries its opaque result or a typed denial. Both cross the same seal
codec and fail-closed port discipline as every other port — there is no second
transport.

Security by construction:

  * Credential material is OPAQUE. A `PublicKeyCredential` is a typed handle
    whose fields are base64url `String` envelopes of buffers the module never
    decodes — there is no accessor that returns raw key bytes, and no `Debug`
    / `Display` path renders them. The relying party server verifies the
    attestation / assertion; this module only carries it.
  * `challenge` and every credential `id` are base64url `String`s at the port
    boundary. The JS sink decodes them to `ArrayBuffer`s for the browser and
    re-encodes every returned buffer, so raw bytes never appear in a frame.
  * A `NotAllowedError`, a user cancellation, or a security refusal becomes a
    typed `Denied`; an absent API becomes `Unavailable`. Neither is ever a
    thrown error or a silently dropped frame — the inbound decoder is total
    and fail-closed.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses
`js-port:web-authn` (import-derived, keyed on the canonical
`Ipe.Browser.WebAuthn` path prefix via `WebCapability::for_browser_module`,
alias-immune); only the top-level app's `[capabilities] accepts` set can grant
it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.WebAuthn.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound
    ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` wiring.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `register` returns a
    `Task Error PublicKeyCredential` for the attestation ceremony, and
    `authenticate` returns one for the assertion ceremony. `results` is the
    inbound subscription for a subscription-shaped wiring; the ceremony `case`
    is EXHAUSTIVE, so a denial or an unavailability becomes a typed value,
    never a dropped frame.

## `CreationOptions`

Registration (attestation) ceremony options — the `publicKey` creation
options for `navigator.credentials.create`.

  * `rpId` / `rpName` — the relying party's id (a registrable domain) and its
    human-readable name.
  * `userId` — a base64url `String` opaque user handle (NOT an email or a
    username): the stable, non-PII id the authenticator stores.
  * `userName` / `userDisplayName` — the account name and display name shown
    during the ceremony.
  * `challenge` — a base64url `String` of the relying party's random
    challenge bytes. It MUST be freshly minted server-side per ceremony; a
    reused or client-chosen challenge defeats the protocol.
  * `algorithms` — the preferred COSE algorithm identifiers (e.g. `-7` for
    ES256, `-257` for RS256), most-preferred first.
  * `timeoutMs` — the ceremony timeout in milliseconds.
  * `userVerification` — `"required"`, `"preferred"`, or `"discouraged"`.

## `RequestOptions`

Authentication (assertion) ceremony options — the `publicKey` request
options for `navigator.credentials.get`.

  * `rpId` — the relying party's id.
  * `challenge` — a base64url `String` of the fresh server challenge (same
    freshness requirement as registration).
  * `allowCredentials` — base64url `String` credential ids the ceremony may
    use; an empty list lets the authenticator choose a resident credential.
  * `timeoutMs` — the ceremony timeout in milliseconds.
  * `userVerification` — `"required"`, `"preferred"`, or `"discouraged"`.

## `PublicKeyCredential`

A completed public-key credential — the typed, opaque handle a ceremony
yields. `id` is the base64url credential id; `rawId` is its base64url raw
form; `response` is the attestation or assertion envelope. The handle carries
ONLY base64url envelopes — no accessor returns raw key material, so a program
can neither forge one nor read a key out of band.

## `AttestationResponse`

The attestation response of a completed registration ceremony. Every field
is a base64url `String` envelope of an opaque buffer the relying party server
verifies — the module never decodes key bytes.

  * `clientDataJson` — the base64url `clientDataJSON`.
  * `attestationObject` — the base64url `attestationObject` carrying the new
    public key and the attestation statement.

## `AssertionResponse`

The assertion response of a completed authentication ceremony. Every field
is a base64url `String` envelope of an opaque buffer.

  * `clientDataJson` — the base64url `clientDataJSON`.
  * `authenticatorData` — the base64url authenticator data.
  * `signature` — the base64url assertion signature. OPAQUE: the module
    carries it to the relying party, never inspects it.
  * `userHandle` — the base64url user handle the authenticator returned, or
    `""` when it returned none.

## `Outcome`

A typed ceremony outcome delivered by the `results` subscription.

  * `Completed credential` — the ceremony returned a credential.
  * `Refused` — the host refused the ceremony (`NotAllowedError`, a user
    cancellation, or a security refusal). Fail-closed, never a throw.
  * `NotAvailable` — the Web Authentication API is absent in this context.

## `register`

```ipe
register : CreationOptions -> Task Error PublicKeyCredential
```

`register opts` — run a registration (attestation) ceremony via
`navigator.credentials.create`, resolving to a `PublicKeyCredential` carrying
the attestation response.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). The served first-party JS
sink (SRI-pinned, the stdlib's) reaches `navigator.credentials.create`; a host
refusal resolves the `Task` to `Error.permissionDenied`, and an absent API to
an `Error.unavailable` — never a panic, never a throw.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:web-authn`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort WebAuthn ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `authenticate`

```ipe
authenticate : RequestOptions -> Task Error PublicKeyCredential
```

`authenticate opts` — run an authentication (assertion) ceremony via
`navigator.credentials.get`, resolving to a `PublicKeyCredential` carrying the
assertion response.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). The served first-party JS
sink reaches `navigator.credentials.get`; a host refusal resolves the `Task`
to `Error.permissionDenied`, and an absent API to an `Error.unavailable`.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:web-authn`; the app must grant it
with `accepts = [ JsPort WebAuthn ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `results`

```ipe
results : (Outcome -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`results toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`, for a
subscription-shaped ceremony flow.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into an `Outcome` —
every variant is covered, so no ceremony frame can ever be silently dropped.

## `credentialId`

```ipe
credentialId : PublicKeyCredential -> String
```

`credentialId credential` — the base64url credential id, the one field a
client reads directly to name the credential. Both a registration and an
authentication carry one.

## `attestation`

```ipe
attestation : PublicKeyCredential -> Maybe AttestationResponse
```

`attestation credential` — the registration `AttestationResponse` envelope,
or `Nothing` when `credential` came from an authentication ceremony. The
relying party server verifies the returned envelope; the client never decodes
its opaque fields.

## `assertion`

```ipe
assertion : PublicKeyCredential -> Maybe AssertionResponse
```

`assertion credential` — the authentication `AssertionResponse` envelope, or
`Nothing` when `credential` came from a registration ceremony. The relying
party server verifies the returned envelope; the client never decodes its
opaque fields.
